record.paper_title: Structural results on circular-arc graphs and circle graphs: A survey and the main open problems
record.original_question: Give forbidden induced subgraph characterizations for the full class of circular-arc graphs and for the full class of circle graphs. Work with simple graphs. An induced subgraph on a chosen vertex set keeps exactly the edges of the original graph whose endpoints both lie in that vertex set. A forbidden induced subgraph characterization asks for a set of graphs F such that a graph belongs to the target class exactly when it contains no induced graph from F. A circular-arc graph is an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle, and a circle graph is an intersection graph of chords on a circle.

evidence.quote: The main structural open problem regarding the classes of circular-arc graphs and circle graphs is that of characterizing them by forbidden induced subgraphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work with finite simple undirected graphs. Given a graph G=(V,E) and a subset S⊆V, the induced subgraph G[S] has vertex set S and edge set {uv∈E : u,v∈S}. Given a family F of graphs, a graph G is F-free if no induced subgraph of G is isomorphic to a member of F. A forbidden induced subgraph characterization of a graph class C is a family F such that a graph belongs to C if and only if it is F-free.

A circular-arc graph is the intersection graph of a family of open arcs of a circle: vertices correspond to arcs, and two vertices are adjacent iff the corresponding arcs intersect.

A circle graph is the intersection graph of a family of chords of a circle: vertices correspond to chords, and two vertices are adjacent iff the corresponding chords cross.

Problem: Exhibit a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for the class of all circular-arc graphs, and exhibit a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for the class of all circle graphs. That is, describe explicit families F_CA and F_C of graphs such that a graph is a circular-arc graph iff it is F_CA-free, and a graph is a circle graph iff it is F_C-free.
artifact.status_search_result: A full forbidden induced subgraph characterization for circular-arc graphs and for circle graphs remains a long-standing open problem. Substantial partial results exist (e.g., characterizations within subclasses such as normal Helly circular-arc graphs, split graphs, and other structural obstruction results like the "blocking quadruple"), but no complete list is known for either class.

status_evidence.title: Blocking Quadruple: A New Obstruction to Circular-Arc Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Finding a forbidden induced subgraph characterization of circular-arc graphs is a long-standing open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem for circular-arc graphs is open; only partial obstructions are known.

status_evidence.title: Forbidden structure characterization of circular-arc graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a structural (walk-based) obstruction characterization rather than a list of forbidden induced subgraphs.
status_evidence.claim: Only structural, not induced-subgraph, characterizations are known so far.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Circular-arc Graphs: I. Split Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Provides forbidden induced subgraph characterization restricted to split graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist within subclasses; the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Forbidden Induced Subgraphs of Normal Helly Circular-Arc Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization and detection for normal Helly circular-arc graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Subclass characterizations are known, but not for the full class.
